correction.text: Middle and Upper Egypt, which the Third Intermediate Period page says the priests ruled "in all but name"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; no Cliopatria row (its Twenty-second Dynasty shape for -800 puts Thebes under the Libyans; the New Kingdom row ends -801). The High Priest page says the priests were "effectively the rulers of Upper Egypt from 1080 to c. 943 BC" and gives no frontier; the Third Intermediate Period page adds Middle Egypt but no boundary. Drawn as the Nile Valley from the Delta apex to the south (Fayyum edge to the Nubian frontier); no area figure. [Author fix 2026-10-19, thin finding on the northern limit] The El-Hibeh page https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El-Hibeh (second look) says the town (ancient Tayu-djayet, 28.787 N 30.921 E) "was a frontier town, marking the division of the country between the High Priests of Amun" and the Tanis kings, from "the late 20th Dynasty to the 22nd Dynasty" (no years), with bricks "stamped with the names of the High Priests Pinedjem I and Menkheperre". The Third Intermediate Period page names no northern limit. If the frontier lay at El-Hibeh, this shape overreaches by the Fayyum and the northern third of Beni Suef governorate (Herakleopolis, c. 29.1 N, would lie north of the line); the shape is kept as the Third Intermediate Period page words it ("Middle and Upper Egypt") because the El-Hibeh page dates the frontier only by dynasty range and gives no line.

region.text: Thebes and Upper Egypt (Middle and Upper Egypt in the Third Intermediate Period page)

ledger.note: 1080: Herihor is proclaimed first ruling High Priest of Amun, in the nineteenth year of Ramesses XI. The page: "proclaimed as the first ruling High Priest of Amun in 1080 BC"; "He ruled in the south in Thebes, while Ramesses XI ruled from the north in Pi-Ramesses"; the priests were de facto rulers, "writing their names in cartouches and being buried in royal tombs".

region.text: Middle and Upper Egypt under the High Priests of Amun at Thebes, the land the Twenty-first Dynasty is recorded (me-03-b) as holding in nominal overlordship

ledger.note: 1077: Ramesses XI dies and Smendes founds the Twenty-first Dynasty at Tanis; the priests of Thebes are then the vassal of Tanis in nominal terms only. The High Priest of Amun page: "Though not officially pharaohs, the High Priests of Amun at Thebes were the de facto rulers of Upper Egypt" and "They are however not regarded as a ruling dynasty with pharaonic prerogatives"; it gives no oath, tribute or other tie to the Tanis kings and does not mention 1077 (page silent). The Third Intermediate Period page (second page) says the priests ruled Middle and Upper Egypt "in all but name" while Smendes I controlled only Lower Egypt. The status is the researcher's reading, written to mirror the vassal_start of me-03-b's Twenty-first Dynasty dossier (-1077, counterpart high-priests-of-amun-at-thebes); the two dossiers must be drawn as one vassal tint, not two. The page also shows the priests drifting toward the throne (Herihor "First High Priest of Amun to claim to be pharaoh", cartouches, royal tombs; Psusennes III or Pinedjem II "the last High Priest of Amun to consider himself as a pharaoh-like figure"), so independence in all but name is the other reading.

region.text: Middle and Upper Egypt, at the end of the priests' rule and of the Tanis kings' nominal overlordship

ledger.note: 943: the Twenty-first Dynasty ends and the priests' rule ends with it. The High Priest of Amun page ends the priestly rule at "c. 943 BC" ("effectively the rulers of Upper Egypt from 1080 to c. 943 BC") and the table's last entry, Psusennes III, runs to 943; Iuput, a son of Shoshenq I, is high priest from 944. Mirrors the vassal_end of me-03-b's Twenty-first Dynasty (-943). The land then passes to the Twenty-second Dynasty (see the dissolve below); how Shoshenq I took Thebes is not on the page.

943: the priest-kings of Thebes end. The table's last entry, Psusennes III, runs to 943 ("effectively the rulers of Upper Egypt from 1080 to c. 943 BC"); Iuput, a son of Shoshenq I, was high priest from 944 (944–924). [Reviewer me-03-x, 2026-10-19] Counterpart twenty-second-dynasty-of-egypt added to mirror me-03-b's gain of -943 from this dossier (Iuput, son of Shoshenq I, high priest from 944).

certainty.note: The pages give no frontier; the division of Egypt between Tanis and Thebes is described only in words. El-Hibeh (Tayu-djayet) is described as the frontier town between the priests and the Tanis kings from the late 20th to the 22nd Dynasty, so the northern limit is probably near 28.8 N; the shape is drawn to the Fayyum, soft.

notes: The priesthood as a state. The 21st Dynasty dossier (me-03-b) treats it as a vassal of Tanis from 1077 to 943 (vassal_start/vassal_end with counterpart high-priests-of-amun-at-thebes); this dossier now writes the mirror (vassal_start -1077 and vassal_end -943, counterpart twenty-first-dynasty-of-egypt, confidence 2: added after the reviewer's blocking finding, 2026-10-19) and supplies the land and the 1080 start, three years earlier than the 21st's 1077, because the page dates Herihor's proclamation to the nineteenth year of Ramesses XI. 1080-1077 the priests are independent of Tanis (Ramesses XI still reigns in the north). The vassal reading is the researcher's: the High Priest page says only that the priests were 'not officially pharaohs' and 'not regarded as a ruling dynasty with pharaonic prerogatives', and describes no tie to the Tanis kings; if the map is to draw them independent, me-03-b would have to drop its pair as well, so the two dossiers must change together.  The Third Intermediate Period page says the division 'was less significant than it seems, since both the priests and pharaohs came from the same family' (flagged there as needing a citation); the High Priest page shows Psusennes I and Psusennes III/II leaving the priesthood for the throne. The ruler table overlaps itself (Pinedjem I 1070–1032, his sons from 1054); the strip is cut to avoid overlap. No page opened dates the priests' hold on Middle Egypt (Herakleopolis). Before Herihor, the Viceroy of Kush Pinehesy besieged Thebes (page, undated).
